title: How to export keynote presentation movie mac: a Keynote 15.4 guide for macOS 26
metaTitle: Export Keynote Presentation as Movie on Mac: Step by Step
description: Export keynote presentation movie mac in Keynote 15.4: use File > Export To > Movie, then set Playback, range, resolution and Advanced Options.
secondaryKeywords: Keynote exported movie not playing video
intro: To export a Keynote presentation as a movie on Mac, open the file and choose File > Export To > Movie. Pick a Playback option, set the slide range and resolution, click Save, then click Export.
tldr: Open the finished deck in the Keynote Mac app, then choose File > Export To > Movie.
Choose Slideshow Recording to include narration you recorded, or Self-Playing for a deck that runs without a presenter.
Set the From slide range, the Resolution, and any Advanced Options before you click Save.
Apple's export guide lists no keyboard shortcut for movie export, so use the menu every time.
Keynote 15.4 for Mac needs macOS 26 or later. Export from the Mac app, not Keynote for iCloud.

blocks.text: Why export a Keynote presentation as a movie

A movie plays anywhere a video file plays. You can email it to someone who doesn't have Keynote, loop it on a display screen, or upload it to a learning platform. Keynote builds the movie from your slides, their timing, and any narration you recorded. Export from Keynote itself, so you don't need a screen recorder.
Check your Keynote version and Mac first

Apple's What's new page lists Keynote 15.4 as the latest version. Keynote 15.4 for Mac requires macOS 26 or later. To check what you have, open Keynote > About Keynote. If the number starts with 14, you're on the older Keynote 14.5 app, which MacRumors reports gets no new features.

Apple's new Creator Studio edition is a separate app, version 15.1 according to MacRumors, and you install it to get new features. Apple's 15.4 notes don't mention any change to movie export or Export To. The most recent export change Apple lists is in 14.4, which added exporting to other formats through Shortcuts. So the steps below should match what you see on 15.4.

Export from the Mac app. Apple's Keynote for iCloud page says recorded narration does not play on iCloud.com, although it stays in the file. I found no Apple page that says iCloud can export a movie, so don't plan this export from the browser.

blocks.title: No shortcut for this export
blocks.text: Apple's export guide lists no keyboard shortcut for movie export. Use File > Export To > Movie every time, and expect to click through the dialog.
The movie export dialog, setting by setting

The dialog has four areas you care about. Playback decides whether narration goes in. From limits the slides. Resolution sets the picture size. Advanced Options holds the rest. The table below lists each setting and where it lives.

blocks.text: Choose Slideshow Recording or Self-Playing for Playback

Playback is the setting that changes the movie most. Slideshow Recording includes any narration you recorded with Play > Record Slideshow. Self-Playing suits a deck that runs without a presenter standing next to it.

Here's how to choose. If you talked over the slides, pick Slideshow Recording. If the deck should run alone on a screen with no voice, pick Self-Playing. Apple lists narration only under Slideshow Recording, so check that option first whenever you recorded a voice.
Export only part of the deck with From

The From option takes a beginning slide and an ending slide. Use it when only part of the deck changed, or when you need one section as its own clip. Keynote remembers the range for the next export, so the fields may already show numbers from last time. Read them before you click Save.

Here is a common case. You updated the middle of a long talk and need a short clip of that section. Enter the slide numbers for that section, export it, then reset the range to the full deck before your next full export.
Resolution, frame rate, and Advanced Options

Resolution is a pop-up menu with presets. Pick the preset that matches where the movie will play. If no preset fits, choose Custom at the bottom of the menu and enter the size yourself. A custom size helps with an unusual display shape, but check it on the real screen.

Advanced Options stays hidden until you expand it. Inside, you'll find frame rate, movie format, color space format, and transparent slide background. Most people can leave these alone. Change frame rate only if the platform you're uploading to asks for one. Leave transparent slide background off unless your slides need to sit over other content.
Record narration before you export

Narration takes a short rehearsal. Open the deck and choose Play > Record Slideshow. Click Start Recording, wait for the 3-second countdown, and start talking. Press Right Arrow to move to the next slide, and Left Arrow to go back.

Use the Mute button when you need to pause the voice mid-talk, such as when a phone rings. Click Start Recording again to stop. If a take goes wrong, choose Play > Clear Recording to remove it, then record again. Apple's recording guide doesn't list a microphone requirement, so test your microphone before a long take.
A worked example: exporting a narrated talk

Say you're giving a short talk, and you want the voice in a movie that a colleague can watch later. Open the deck, choose Play > Record Slideshow, and record the talk slide by slide. Click Start Recording again when you finish.

Next, choose File > Export To > Movie. Set Playback to Slideshow Recording, set the From range to cover the whole deck, and pick a Resolution preset that suits a laptop screen. Click Save, name the file, choose a folder, and click Export.
Finally, open the movie in QuickTime Player and watch the first and last slides. If the voice cuts off at the end, record that last slide again, then export the movie again.
Common mistakes that waste a movie export

items: Picking Self-Playing when you wanted your voice in the movie. Slideshow Recording is the option that includes recorded narration.
Typing a file extension in the name box. Apple's steps say to leave it off and type the name only.
Forgetting the From range you used last time, so the movie starts late or stops early.
Looking for a keyboard shortcut. Apple lists none for movie export.
Starting from Keynote for iCloud. Recorded narration does not play there.
Skipping the watch-through. Play the file in QuickTime Player before you send it.

blocks.text: Embedded videos that stutter or repeat the first frame

Some exports show a video that stutters or repeats its first frame. A 2023 Apple Community thread about Keynote 13.2 describes that problem. The original poster re-encoded the embedded videos with HandBrake to H.264, then replaced them in a duplicate of the file. The thread shows no Apple response.

Treat that workaround as a lead, not a confirmed fix. The report is from 13.2, and this guide covers 15.4. Work on a copy of the deck, re-encode the clip, swap it in, and export again. Then watch the start of each video in the movie before you share it.
Do you need Apple Creator Studio for movie export?

Apple's Creator Studio page says Keynote, Pages, Numbers, and Freeform remain free for everyone. The paid plan costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year after a one-month free trial for new subscribers. It adds premium templates, a royalty-free media library, and intelligence features.

The page does not say which Keynote features need the subscription. Apple's movie export guide does not mention a subscription either. Start with the free Keynote app, and check the menus on your own Mac.
Check the movie before you send it

Open the exported movie in QuickTime Player and watch it end to end. Listen for narration that starts late or cuts off. Check that each slide holds for as long as you meant it to. Look closely at the first frame of any embedded video.

If you show the movie to a group, play it on the device they'll use. Screen size and audio output change how a movie feels. Keep the Keynote file too. When a slide changes, export a new movie rather than trying to fix the old one.
Where Lazur fits when you get stuck

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. It doesn't export the movie for you. It points at things on your screen, explains them out loud, and guides you one click at a time when you ask how to do something.

Hold Option and Command together, then ask a question about what's on screen. Ask where the export option is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask to be walked through the dialog, and Lazur waits for each click before the next step. You still make every click yourself.
What to do after your movie is exported

If the deck still needs notes for yourself, read [how to add presenter notes in Keynote on Mac](/how-to/add-presenter-notes-in-keynote) before you record. Teachers who build lesson slides can look at [Keynote for teachers on Mac](/for/teachers/keynote). If you want to ask questions while you work, see the [Keynote page for Lazur](/apps/keynote).
Write down the Playback, range, resolution, and Advanced Options you used. Next time, you can repeat the export without working out the settings again.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to export a Keynote presentation as a movie?
faq.answer: Not in Apple's export guide. Apple lists no keyboard shortcut for movie export, so use File > Export To > Movie each time. The shortcuts Apple documents for recording are Right Arrow and Left Arrow, and those move you through slides while you narrate.

faq.question: Does the exported movie include my narration?
faq.answer: Only if you choose Slideshow Recording under Playback. Record the narration first with Play > Record Slideshow, then export with Slideshow Recording selected.

faq.question: Can I export only some of the slides?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the From option in the movie export dialog and enter the beginning and ending slide numbers. Keynote remembers that range for your next export, so check it before you click Save.

faq.question: Can I export the movie from Keynote for iCloud?
faq.answer: Apple's iCloud page says recorded narration does not play on iCloud.com. I found no Apple page that confirms movie export on iCloud.com, so use the Keynote Mac app for this export.

faq.question: Do I need an Apple Creator Studio subscription to export a movie?
faq.answer: Apple's Creator Studio page says Keynote stays free for everyone. It does not say which features need the paid plan, and Apple's export guide does not mention a subscription.

faq.question: Why does an embedded video freeze in my exported movie?
faq.answer: A 2023 Apple Community thread about Keynote 13.2 reports stutter and a repeated first frame with embedded videos. The workaround there was to re-encode the video with HandBrake using H.264 and replace it in a copy of the file. Apple did not reply in that thread, so test the result before you rely on it.

faq.question: Which Keynote version do I need for these steps?
faq.answer: Apple's What's new page lists Keynote 15.4 as the latest version, and it requires macOS 26 or later. Check your version under Keynote > About Keynote. Keynote 14.5 is the older app and gets no new features.

faq.question: Can Lazur export the movie for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur points at the Export To menu, explains the options, and guides you one click at a time. It does not click buttons or work in other apps for you, so you make each click.

task: Export a Keynote presentation as a movie on Mac
appliesTo: Keynote 15.4 for Mac, macOS 26 or later
requirements: Keynote 15.4 for Mac, which requires macOS 26 or later
A finished presentation open in the Keynote Mac app
A working microphone, if you want to record narration

steps.name: Open the finished deck
steps.text: Open the finished presentation in the Keynote app on your Mac. Read each slide once more and check any embedded videos. Export from the Mac app, not from Keynote for iCloud.
steps.tip: Keynote for iCloud does not play recorded narration, so it is the wrong place to start this export.

steps.name: Record narration (optional)
steps.text: If you want your voice in the movie, record it first. Choose Play > Record Slideshow, then click Start Recording. Wait for the 3-second countdown, then move through the slides with Right Arrow. Click Start Recording again to stop.
steps.tip: Use Left Arrow to go back a slide, and the Mute button to pause narration during a break.

steps.name: Open the movie export
steps.text: Choose File > Export To > Movie. The movie options open. Apple's export guide lists no keyboard shortcut for this, so you use the menu each time.
steps.tip: If you can't find Export To, make sure the deck window is active and the File menu is open.

steps.name: Choose Playback
steps.text: Under Playback, pick Slideshow Recording to include recorded narration. Pick Self-Playing for a deck that runs without a presenter.
steps.tip: Choose Slideshow Recording first if you recorded a voice.

steps.name: Set the From range (optional)
steps.text: Type the beginning and ending slide numbers to export only part of the deck. Keynote remembers the range for the next export, so check the fields even if you didn't type anything.
steps.tip: Reset the range to the full deck before you export the whole presentation.

steps.name: Pick a Resolution
steps.text: Open the Resolution pop-up menu and choose a preset that suits where the movie will play. For a custom size, choose Custom at the bottom of the menu and enter your own size.
steps.tip: Check the movie on the real screen. A preset that looks right on a laptop may not suit a wall display.

steps.name: Expand Advanced Options
steps.text: Click Advanced Options to show frame rate, movie format, color space format, and transparent slide background. Change only the settings your destination needs.
steps.tip: Leave transparent slide background off unless your slides must sit over other content.

steps.name: Click Save and name the file
steps.text: Click Save. Type the file name without the file extension, add tags if you use them, then choose a folder from the Where pop-up menu.
steps.tip: Leave the extension off the name. Apple's steps say to type the name only.

steps.name: Click Export and check the result
steps.text: Click Export and keep Keynote open until the movie is finished. Open the file in QuickTime Player and watch it through.
steps.tip: Watch the start for frozen frames and the end for narration that gets cut off.

troubleshooting.problem: The exported movie has no narration
troubleshooting.fix: Check Playback. Only Slideshow Recording includes recorded narration. If the voice never made it into the deck, record again with Play > Record Slideshow, then export with Slideshow Recording selected.

troubleshooting.problem: The movie starts or stops on the wrong slides
troubleshooting.fix: Reopen the export dialog and check the From range. Keynote remembers your last range, so reset it to the slides you need before you click Save.

troubleshooting.problem: Embedded video stutters or repeats the first frame
troubleshooting.fix: A 2023 thread about Keynote 13.2 reports this, and the workaround was to re-encode the video with HandBrake using H.264 and replace it in a copy of the deck. Apple did not confirm a fix in that thread, so test the result.

troubleshooting.problem: Your Keynote menus differ from this guide
troubleshooting.fix: Check Keynote > About Keynote. Keynote 14.5 is the older app and gets no new features. Use the current 15.x version for these steps. MacRumors reports the new Creator Studio edition is version 15.1, a separate app.

troubleshooting.problem: The movie looks wrong on the target screen
troubleshooting.fix: Compare the Resolution preset with the screen it will play on. If no preset fits, choose Custom at the bottom of the Resolution menu and enter the size your display needs, then export again.
